corrections.form_value: Data, code, Dutch-to-English translations, data cleaning steps, rating protocols, categorization protocols, and the Monte Carlo prompt/parameter optimization studies. The main text gives regression coefficients with SEs but no arm means or SDs except as bar charts (Figures 2 to 6).

confirmed: Read the complete 165-line markdown conversion and all 5 PDF pages, including references, acknowledgements and author contributions; there is no appended supplement in this PDF (PDF pp. 1-5).

The stored source is the five-page arXiv paper identified in retrieval.json; no version number is printed in the PDF, and p. 5 refers to the camera ready paper. The arXiv API identifies 2206.08932v1, published 2022-06-10, and states acceptance as an ICCC 2022 Short Paper (https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2206.08932, entry id, published and arxiv:comment).
The title and all five named authors agree with the document header (PDF p. 1).

design_class and context_class are correctly ai_vs_human, and core is correctly no: previously collected human responses were compared with GPT-3-generated responses. The two preliminary Monte Carlo experiments optimized GPT-3 engines/prompts/parameters and were not randomized AI-assistance studies of people (PDF p. 2, Methods: Sample and Materials).

The human sample comprised 42 Dutch-fluent University of Amsterdam students and 823 responses before cleaning; 42 humans and 774 responses remained in the analysis. GPT-3 supplied 820 responses from 144 runs before cleaning, with 781 responses from 144 runs analyzed; n_randomized is appropriately null (PDF p. 2, Sample and Materials; p. 3, Results opening paragraph).

The response total n_units = 1555 is the arithmetic sum 774 + 781, explicitly shown in the form; the PDF prints the two component counts rather than a combined total. These are responses, not people (PDF p. 3, Results opening paragraph).

The human AUT used book, fork and tin can, with two minutes per object. The paper names davinci-002, temperature sampled from .65 to .80, frequency and presence penalties both 1, and two collection sessions (PDF p. 2, Materials).

Two trained judges were blinded to response source and used a 5-point scale; after removing invalid/incomplete responses, ICCs were .78 for originality, .70 for utility and .79 for surprise. Semantic distance was 1 minus cosine similarity, using spaCy en_core_web_lg (PDF p. 2, Procedure).
Originality: humans higher, β=.17, SE = .06, z = 2.91, p = .004; the reported string and one-line finding agree (PDF p. 3, Results, originality/usefulness/surprise subsection; Figure 2).
Utility: GPT-3 higher, β=-.55, SE = .06, z = -8.52, p<.001; the reported string and one-line finding agree (PDF p. 3, same Results subsection; Figure 5 on p. 4).
Surprise: humans higher, β=.14, SE = .07, z = 1.96, p = .050; the reported string and one-line finding agree, including the printed p = .050 (PDF p. 3, same Results subsection; Figure 3).

Semantic distance: humans higher, β= .10, SE = . 02, z = 5.45, p<.001; the reported string and one-line finding agree. These regression models used response-level outcomes while accounting for responses within a person or GPT-3 run and adjusting for AUT object (PDF p. 3, same Results subsection; Figure 4).

Flexibility was computed only for tin can in the reported comparison: humans higher, F(1, 85) = 5.53, p = .021, with greater variance for GPT-3. The number of response sets is not stated; keeping n_units null is appropriate (PDF p. 3, flexibility Results subsection; Figure 6 on p. 4).

Flexibility divides the number of represented categories by the number of responses within an individual response set; it is not across-person diversity. All five question fields are appropriately none for this AI-versus-human comparison (PDF p. 2, Procedure; creativity-codebook.md, section 6; form-spec.md, question field note).

The form correctly flags the source inconsistency: the reliability paragraph says approximately 10% of 1656 responses, whereas the stated pre-cleaning counts are 823 human and 820 GPT-3 responses, summing to 1643. No explanation appears in the document (PDF p. 2, Sample, Materials and Procedure).
This is an original output-comparison study, not a synthesis; null synthesis counts and an empty pooled-estimate list are appropriate (PDF pp. 2-3, Methods and Results).
summary: The design, counts, and all five reported results match the source; no people were randomized to AI assistance. Six corrections address blank eligibility fields, missing statistic-availability labels and data/code links, and the description of Figure 6.
